title: Benchmark-fix reversal on 15m: buy a pre-fix drop at the 4pm London and 4pm New York bitcoin reference-rate strikes

source.title: Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns Around the Clock (Krohn, Mueller, Whelan; BoC SWP 2021-48, Journal of Finance 2024)

rule_summary: 15m closed bars; signal at a bar close, fill at the next open. Two fixes per day, local clock with DST: LONDON fix = 16:00 Europe/London (every day); NY fix = 16:00 America/New_York (Monday-Friday only). For each fix, the pre-fix window is the 8 bars opening 14:00 to 15:45 local. P0 = open of the 14:00 bar; Cpre = close of the 15:45 bar; r = Cpre/P0 - 1. s = sample std of 15m log returns over the previous 2880 bars times sqrt(8). ENTRY at the close of the 15:45 local bar if r <= -max(0.005, 0.75*s) and flat; buy at the open of the 16:00 bar (the strike). EXIT, first of: take-profit when price reaches P0 (full retrace of the pre-fix drop); stop at entry*(1 - max(0.01, |r|)); time exit at the close of the 16th bar after entry (4 hours). At most one trade per fix; no trend filter, no higher-timeframe data.
mechanism: Krohn, Mueller and Whelan show that FX returns drift before the big benchmark fixings and reverse after them: dealers who must deliver at the fix pre-hedge and warehouse inventory, then unload it to later counterparties, so the pre-fix move is uninformed price pressure that reverts. Crypto has the same structure: the CME CF BRR strikes at 4pm London from a 3-4pm window and settles CME futures, and BRRNY (3-4pm New York) sets NAV for US spot ETFs (learnbitcoin.com glossary), so APs and hedgers trade a fixed window regardless of value. The long side buys after that flow has pushed price down and earns the post-fix rebound from the liquidity provider's side. Only drops of at least 0.5% and 0.75 sigma qualify, and the target is the full pre-fix retrace, so the planned gross move is above 0.5%; the stop is at least 1%.
